findings.issue: The PRIVILEGED probe set is a hand-written list of role strings. decide() calls any rule that neither anonymous, ROLE_CUSTOMER nor one of these six authorities passes DENY. rolePrefixesAreKnown (AC-9) only compares roleRules(), and nothing pins the set of DENY entries. So a future edge rule that uses a role outside this list (for example a new Roles.WAREHOUSE) shows up as an unchecked DENY and AC-9 does not fail. AC-9's wording covers 'any other prefix whose rule is not plain authenticated'. A rule like hasRole("CUSTOMER") on a prefix is also read as AUTHENTICATED and is not flagged. Neither case opens an exposure, because both are more restrictive, but the drift goes unnoticed.
findings.fix: In rolePrefixesAreKnown, assert the full map of entries whose kind is not PERMIT or AUTHENTICATED (expect {/actuator/** -> DENY, /api/admin/** -> ROLE[4]}), so any new DENY or unknown-role rule fails. Build PRIVILEGED from the Roles.ROLE_* constants instead of string literals.

findings.issue: Any mapping whose matcher is not an OrServerWebExchangeMatcher is recorded as the catch-all (catchAll=true, matches everything). The self-check only looks at the last entry. A future .matchers(customMatcher) in the middle of the chain would therefore be silently read as match-everything and would shadow later rules in classify(). AC-3 and AC-5 row selection and the classification table would then be wrong, with no loud failure (unless the rule is a PERMIT, which AC-12 catches as 'ANY <any exchange>').
findings.fix: Allow a non-Or matcher only at the last index, and otherwise throw IllegalStateException("EdgeRules could not read the chain: unsupported matcher <class> at index i"). Add an EdgeRulesTest case for this.

findings.issue: CUSTOMER, ADMIN, SUPPORT, FINANCE, CATALOG_MANAGER and SELLER tokens are minted once in static fields when the class loads, before the Spring context boots. TestKeys gives them a 600 s lifetime. The class sends about 1266 requests. A normal run takes about 57 s, but evidence.md records a full-class run that hung for more than 10 minutes on a cold docker. On a slow CI agent, every role and CUSTOMER row after minute 10 would fail with 401, which is a timing-dependent false failure.
findings.fix: Mint tokens lazily per test (for example a token(role) call inside each dynamic test or @BeforeEach), or mint them with a lifetime well beyond any plausible class runtime.

findings.issue: field() and hasField() hand-roll a walk up the class hierarchy, and the two functions duplicate each other. Spring's ReflectionUtils.findField(Class, String) already does this walk, and the test already depends on spring-core.
findings.fix: Use ReflectionUtils.findField(target.getClass(), name). Treat null as missing and throw the 'EdgeRules could not read the chain' message, then read the value with ReflectionUtils.makeAccessible + getField (or keep ReflectionTestUtils.getField).

findings.issue: Entry stores only getPatternString() and re-parses it with a new PathPatternParser on every match, so classify() can in principle disagree with the matcher that actually runs (for example if Security ever builds its PathPattern with different parser options). The real PathPattern object is already in hand in readEntries.
findings.fix: Store the reflected PathPattern in Entry and match with it directly. Keep the string only for display and the reviewed-permit keys.

findings.issue: The 2026-11-17 Progress line in TD-P9-01 still lists 'the gateway route contract' as untested, while the Fix line now says it is done.
findings.fix: Add 'Progress 2026-11-25: gateway route contract covered by RouteAuthorizationContractTest (F-20261119-17)', or drop the phrase from the open-items list.

summary: The change is test-only: no src/main or build.gradle file appears in the diff, and the javadoc references in SecurityConfig.java:39 and application.yml:11 now resolve to the new class. It meets its contract. RouteTable binds the routes from the real application.yml with Boot's YamlPropertySourceLoader/Binder into SCG RouteDefinition, so the framework does the comma split. It cross-checks the ids against the live GatewayProperties and fails loudly on zero routes, a route with no Path predicate, or a non-Path predicate. EdgeRules reads the ordered matchers from the AuthorizationWebFilter that actually runs and gets each decision by calling the rule's own ReactiveAuthorizationManager. It is fenced by a self-check: PUBLIC_PATHS reflected and each entry required as an ANY PERMIT, /actuator/** DENY, /api/admin/** ROLE, and a final authenticated catch-all, with every failure reading 'EdgeRules could not read the chain'. EdgeRulesTest unit-tests that self-check. The test is not vacuous. A new permitAll fails AC-12 against the 44-entry REVIEWED_PERMITS list, whose reasons are specific and meaningful. An unrouted PUBLIC_PATHS entry fails AC-6/7. A role-set change fails AC-9 and the AC-8 rows. All three mutation runs are recorded in evidence.md with their failure messages, followed by a green forge-verify run, and every factory asserts that it generated rows and hit named anchors. Behavioural probes go through a real Netty port with real RS256 tokens, a local JWKS stub, mocked Redis and Eureka off. Ports are random, so there is no port clash. The register edits are correct and follow project.md: the TD-TEST-04 section and its index row are removed, the README note and phase9 reference are reworded with no dangling anchor, and remediation-plan row 57 is added with the Q1 seller flag. All findings are minor or nit: (1) DENY entries and roles outside the hard-coded probe list are not pinned by AC-9; (2) a non-Or matcher in the middle of the chain would be silently read as the catch-all; (3) static tokens with a 600 s lifetime are a latent timing flake on very slow runs; (4) field()/hasField() hand-roll what ReflectionUtils.findField already does; (5) the PathPattern is re-parsed instead of reusing the stored object; (6) a stale progress phrase in phase9.md. None of them blocks approval.
